title: Monks Mound, Cahokia
summary: Monks Mound is the largest earthen mound in North America, the central platform of the Mississippian city of Cahokia in present-day Illinois. It rose in a series of stages mostly between about 950 and 1200 CE, reaching roughly 30 m in four terraces. Newer soil studies suggest it may have been built much faster than once thought.

uncertainty.note: Start follows the site marker 'mostly from AD 950-1200' (later enlarged to AD 1250). A 2015 study (reported by the Archaeological Conservancy) argues for a very short build; the start therefore runs 950 to about 1050. End is the present: the mound stands.

phases.description: Built in a series of stages, mostly AD 950-1200; core drilling suggests eight to 14 stages. A 2015 study suggests a much shorter build.
Mound stands as an earthen mass; slopes began to collapse in 2005 and were repaired.

reviewer_note: Shape stepped_pyramid (four terraces) rather than mound. Least sure of the date: the marker text (class other) says 950-1200 and an Archaeological Conservancy report on a 2015 study favours a short chronology starting about 1050 or later, so 950 is the older, longer model. Height and base are the Cahokia Mounds Museum Society's figures; base depends on the contour used (291 x 236 m at 130 m, 320 x 294 m at 128 m). UNESCO's own text says 30 m, fourteen stages, four terraces.
